doc.title: Plas Johnson interviewed by Monk Rowe, Sarasota, Florida, April 12, 1996

chapter: Opening and arrival in Los Angeles
title: Black music and the white teenage audience
summary: Blues artists and gospel-style groups popular in the black community and increasingly with white teenagers.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: And a lot of them were playing black music that the white teenager started to like. Is that correct?

Sure. The blues artists were like Charles Brown, Amos Millburn, Roy Milton, some of the singing groups — Clyde McPhatter and the Drifters, they had an upbeat type of Gospel quartet. And they were quite popular in the black community also.
When you got to L.A. then you started playing on rhythm & blues and — was it rock & roll yet? Was it called rock & roll?
